lens: The evidence uncovers a sexual dimorphism paradox: caloric restriction selectively inhibits intestinal adenomas in male but not female Apc-mutant mice, while simultaneously triggering uniform metabolic and proteomic shifts in both sexes, challenging the assumption of gender-agnostic dietary benefits.
known_to_ignore: Caloric restriction universally reduces body weight and improves metabolic health markers
CR is a well-established intervention for extending lifespan in model organisms
tensions: Fact 31457 shows visceral fat removal attenuates macroadenomas in female Apc(1638N/+) mice, but caloric restriction does not, while fact 31458 demonstrates the opposite sex-specific pattern for CR's efficacy
Fact 3314 indicates CR dramatically elevates bone marrow adiposity in male C57Bl/6J mice, conflicting with its potential bone-protective effects suggested by lowered leptin and IGF-1 in fact 3312
gaps: Interaction effects between caloric restriction and visceral fat removal in both sexes simultaneously
Long-term skeletal health outcomes of CR in female mouse models
Role of sex hormones in mediating CR's divergent anti-tumor effects

theses.title: Sexual Dimorphism in Caloric Restriction Efficacy for Intestinal Adenoma Prevention: Mechanistic Insights from Apc-Mutant Mice
theses.rationale: This review would consolidate the striking sex-specific responses to CR in cancer models, arguing for mechanistic studies on hormonal or adipose-tissue pathways to inform gender-tailored cancer prevention strategies.

reviewer_objections: The evidence for sex-specific cancer effects relies on a single 2013 study using Apc(1638N/+) mice, which may not generalize to other cancer models or human populations
Cited facts cover disparate outcomes (cancer, bone metabolism, proteomics) with different mouse strains and interventions, complicating coherent synthesis
next_extractions: Investigate the impact of sex hormone modulation on CR's effects in Apc-mutant models
Study longitudinal bone health parameters under CR in female mice
Explore CR interactions with exercise in sex-specific cancer prevention
